answer: A useful defense is a rate-limited, stake-backed reputation registry: each agent must lock tokens before it can place bids, and its stake is slashed when a randomly audited task proves fraudulent. Reputation and bidding limits attach to the registry entry, so creating fresh identities does not instantly grant trusted capacity; an attacker must fund many deposits and risk losing them. The basalt, oasis, and onyx labels can distinguish task classes, but do not themselves establish identity.
